summary: Govind Vishnu Kathavate was an Indologist. He succeeded Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar to the Sanskrit chair at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt was an Indologist. He served as a professor at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (attested 1933–1939) and succeeded Benoytosh Bhattacharyya as Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1953–1957).

Grace S. Fong is a Sinologist who studied at McGill University and the University of British Columbia. She was a professor at Smith College (~1985–1988) and became associate professor and chair of East Asian Studies at McGill (~1993).

Graeme MacQueen was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his doctorate at Harvard University (~1970–1978) under Masatoshi Nagatomi and served as a lecturer at McMaster University (~1978–2013).

Grafton Elliot Smith was a scholar in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at Sydney Medical School, the University of Sydney, and St John's College, later holding a post at University College London (~1919–1936).
Graham E. Clarke worked in Tibetology and other fields. He held posts at the Institute of Development Studies and at the University of Oxford, where he was a Senior Member (attested 1998).
Graham Lock is a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied under teachers Hsuan Hua and Saddhaloka Bhikkhu.

Graham Parkes is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology who completed his Ph.D. at UC Berkeley (~1973–1979). He served as Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaiʻi (~1979–2008) and held multiple leadership chairs at University College Cork (~2008–2016).

Graham Priest is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Cambridge, LSE (under John Lane Bell), and Melbourne. He held posts at Melbourne (~2001–2009), St Andrews (~2007–2017), and CUNY Graduate Center (~2009).

Sir Graves Champney Haughton was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Fort William College. He was Professor of Hindú Literature and the History of Asia at East India Company College (1819–1827) and secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1831–1832).

Gray Tuttle works in Tibetology, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He earned his Ph.D. from Harvard in 2002 under Leonard van der Kuijp, William C. Kirby, and Philip A. Kuhn, later becoming associate professor at Columbia University (attested 2008–2015).
Graziadio Isaia Ascoli was a linguist and Indologist who founded Archivio glottologico italiano in 1873. He served as a professor at Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano from 1861 to 1902.

Greg Bailey is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Melbourne under J. Durham and studied under Madeleine Biardeau. He was a professor at La Trobe University (attested 2003–2004) and a visiting research fellow at Tübingen (1998).

Gregor Ahn is a religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian scholar who completed his Magister, PhD, and Habilitation at the University of Bonn, studying under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit. He has served as Professor für Vergleichende Religionswissenschaft at Heidelberg University since 1996.

Gregory Forgues is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2011, he studied at the University of Vienna under MA supervisor Helmut Tauscher, teacher Birgit Kellner, and several traditional teachers including Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse and Namkhai Norbu.

Gregory Max Seton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed master's degrees at Naropa University and UC Santa Barbara, and a D.Phil at Wolfson College, Oxford (2015), supervised by Vesna Wallace and Alexis Sanderson.
Gregory Nagy is a scholar of linguistics and other fields. He studied at Indiana University (~1958–1962) and Harvard University (~1962–1966), later taking up a post at Harvard University (~1969).

Gregory P. A. Levine is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history who studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University. In ~2001, he joined UC Berkeley as Associate Professor of Japanese art, architecture, and Buddhist visual cultures.

Gregory Price Grieve is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from the University of Chicago. He held lecturer posts at Chicago and DePaul before becoming Professor and Department Head at UNC Greensboro (2002).

Gregory Schopen is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana. He held professorships at the University of Texas at Austin and UCLA, among other posts.
